# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 11

**1** He replied to me and said: "Hear and understand everything. Those stones which were taken from the plain and placed in the building — the square and white ones which fit their joints — these are the apostles and bishops and teachers and deacons who walked according to the holiness of God, and served as bishop and teacher and deacon in purity and reverence for the elect of God. Some of them have already fallen asleep and some are still living; and they always agreed with one another, and they had peace among themselves and listened to one another. On this account their joints fit together in the building of the tower." **2** "Those which were dragged from the deep sea and placed in the building — who are they? These are those who suffered for the name of the Lord." **3** "And those which were brought from the mountains — who are they?" "These are those who are not new in the faith, and those who were found to be believers through all their lives, and those who are honored among the people of God. **4** But those from the twelve mountains — from the first mountain, which was black — these are the apostates and betrayers of the church, and the blasphemers of the Lord in their sins, and they are ashamed of the name of the Lord. These therefore are dead to God; they cannot be placed in the building. They are of no use in the building. **5** Those from the second mountain, which was bare — these are the hypocrites and the teachers of wickedness, and those who corrupt the servants of God, especially those who are sinners; and these do not have the repentance to go upward, but they have blasphemous words in their mouth. They are stones of the building, but only barely."

---

*EMET note: Vision 3.11 begins the interpretation of the twelve mountains. Mountains 1-2 are the worst categories — apostates/blasphemers and corrupt teachers. The 12-mountain typology is a comprehensive sociology of the early church.*
